source_title: ‘RSS Friends’ registers in U.S. to step up outreach, correct inaccuracies - The Hindu
source_excerpt: Washington A group of RSS well-wishers has registered with the U.S. Department of Justice as a foreign agent of the organisation, aiming to step up outreach in the U.S. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/rashtriya-swayamsevak-sangh-rss/ The RSS Friends, which provided a Georgia address in the registration document, listed Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, Keshavkunj, New Delhi as its “foreign principal”. USCIRF seeks sanctions against RSS, no high-level meetings with its leaders USCIRF seeks sanctions against RSS, no high-level meetings with its leaders The remarks of the religious freedom body’s chief came weeks ahead of RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat’s visit to the U.S. USCIRF seeks sanctions against RSS, no high-level meetings with its leaders storyline 1 The RSS Friends registered with the Department of Justice under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) on August 27. Correcting or responding to information that RSS Friends believes is inaccurate, incomplete, or lacking relevant context is also listed among proposed activities. “RSS Friends does not have a written employment, consulting, lobbying, public-relations, or agency agreement with RSS containing specified deliverables, compensation, or detailed operational instructions,” the group said. Mohan Bhagwat's New York event organised in spirit of open dialogue, says RSS Mohan Bhagwat's New York event organised in spirit of open dialogue, says RSS The remark comes amid a row over the RSS chief’s visit to the U.S. with several American interfaith and civil rights organisations opposing his planned appearance at the Madison Square Garden event Mohan Bhagwat's New York event organised in spirit of open dialogue, says RSS storyline 1 It said the absence of a written contract should not be understood as a representation that no relationship, request, understanding, coordination, authorisation, direction, or other relevant factual connection exists. “RSS Friends will disclose the actual facts relevant to its activities,” it said. The group said its proposed activities are primarily informational, educational, public-relations, and community engagement activities. “Consistent with its governing documents and applicable law, it may communicate with members of the public, journalists, media organisations, researchers, academic and policy institutions, community leaders, civil-society organisations, and, where appropriate, government agencies or officials,” the group said. RSS Friends lists Rajendra Sonarikar, Jayant Pant and Devananda Gaddam as its Board of Directors. Organising or participating in educational, cultural, community, or informational events; communicating, when appropriate and consistent with applicable law, with administrative entities, public agencies, or policymakers regarding factual information or perspectives concerning RSS or matters relevant to the organisation’s stated purposes is listed among the group’s proposed activities. The registration of RSS Friends was submitted two days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s outreach programme Universal Oneness Celebration at New York’s Madison Square Garden on August 29. The event was organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD) Forum.
